name: news_search
description: Current news stories, with REAL publisher URLs and REAL article photos. TWO MODES. (1) Leave `topic` EMPTY for TODAY'S TOP HEADLINES: these come from editorial front pages (Google News plus NYT/BBC/NPR/ABC), ranked by how many independent newsrooms led with the same story, and optionally narrowed with `category`. An empty topic is a VALID request and is the RIGHT way to ask for the top stories — do NOT search for the words 'top stories', which matches roundup pages containing that phrase rather than the news. (2) Give a `topic` to SEARCH: this rotates across keyed providers (gnews, worldnewsapi, currentsapi, thenewsapi, newsapi) so no single provider's daily limit blocks a request. Prefer this tool over a generic web search for anything time-sensitive: web search returns news-site homepages rather than stories. Each item carries {title, url, image, source, snippet, date}; top-headline items also carry {category, consensus, stub}. `consensus` is how many newsrooms carried the story — 2 or more means it is genuinely a top story. `stub: true` marks a Google redirect link: it is safe to SHOW and to link, but it has no article photo and must NOT be scraped. Results default to the US; pass country='gb'/'in'/etc for another market, or country='' for worldwide. An empty items list means no source had a usable story, not an error.

topic.description: What to find stories about, e.g. 'James Webb space telescope' or 'federal reserve rate decision'. Multi-word topics are matched as a phrase. LEAVE EMPTY (or omit) to get today's top headlines instead of a keyword search.

limit.description: How many stories to return (default 6, max 30). Some keyed free tiers cap lower and will return fewer.

country.description: Two-letter region for the news lookup, e.g. 'us', 'gb', 'in'. Defaults to 'us'. Pass an empty string for worldwide. This is a REGION filter, not a language one: the providers are already English-only, and English-language outlets from any country match a generic query, so 'stock market' without a country returns whichever market publishes the most English copy.

category.description: Section for the TOP-HEADLINES mode (only meaningful when `topic` is empty). Omit or use 'top' for a front page blending US, world, business and technology. Ignored when `topic` is given.
